newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil, jet fly way over five-year high.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil, jet fly way over five-year high.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and jet fuel prices soared way over their previous five-year peaks on concerns of higher demand and tight supplies during the current cold season, traders said.

The rise in crudes as well as a $3.25 a tonne increase in gas oil futures on the International Petroleum Exchange lifted Asian prices. Winter demand coincided with China's year-end rush for gas oil ahead of February's Lunar New Year break which saw its imports surging to 600,000 tonnes a month in November and December. Physical gas oil traded at a new post Gulf War peak of $33 a barrel over the previous record last week at $31.80.

A European major sold 220,000 barrels to a Singapore trader for Dec 30-Jan 3 lifting fob. Traders said the rally on swaps boosted physical values. December swaps traded at $32.95 while January traded at $31.90, up $1 over Wednesday. Jet fuel rallied on demand from Indonesia, Japan and S.Korea with 130,000 barrels traded at a five-year high of $34.20, over the last high of $33.75 in January.
The seller was a US major to a Dutch trader, who bought the last cargo at $31.95.
Light distillate was quiet watching Japan naphtha rising by $3-$4 a tonne to $237/$238.50 for first-half February open-spec.

Traders were nervous about the narrowing gasoline/naphtha spread, now quoted at $1 a barrel on spot assessments. A major bid for 50,000-75,000 barrels of 95-octane gasoline at $25.40, lifting Dec 25-Jan 3 fob, below the $25.60 deal reported Tuesday before crude's hikes. Another major, concerned about low prices which are equivalent to 40 cents over naphtha quotes, offered at $3.50 a barrel premium. But the major bought the cargo at the fixed price from a Japanese trader. A Thai refiner's 250,000 barrel-cargo of 95-octane lifting first half January was heard sold at 20 cents over Singapore quotes fob Sri Racha, rumoured sold within the country. -- Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3084)
